text: Which model does NOT need feature scaling?
explain: Trees split one feature at a threshold, so rescaling a feature does not change the splits.

text: A 'city' column has 30 unordered values. Best encoding for logistic regression?
explain: Label codes invent a fake order (Paris < Rome); one-hot gives each city its own 0/1 column.

text: Only 2% of rows are positive. Good first fix for LogisticRegression?
explain: Errors on the rare class get more weight, so the model can't just ignore it; then tune the threshold.

text: A sensor time series has gaps. Which fill uses NO future values?
explain: Forward-fill only looks back; the others peek at later values you won't have at prediction time.

text: Predicting pneumonia at hospital admission. Which feature is target leakage?
explain: It is recorded after the diagnosis, so it encodes the answer and won't exist when you predict.

text: 95% of samples are negative. A model always predicts 'negative'. Accuracy?
explain: Accuracy equals the majority share (the baseline to beat), so on imbalanced data use F1 or ROC-AUC.

text: 100 real positives. The model flags 120 items; 80 of them are real positives. Recall?
explain: Recall = TP / all real positives = 80/100. Precision would be 80/120 ≈ 0.67.

text: You lower the decision threshold from 0.5 to 0.2. What usually happens?
options: Both precision and recall go up
explain: More items are flagged positive: you catch more real positives but also raise more false alarms.

text: Regression target has a few huge outliers. Which metric is least affected by them?
explain: MAE grows linearly with the error; MSE, RMSE and R² square it, so outliers dominate.

text: ROC-AUC = 0.9 means…
options: A random positive outranks a random negative 90% of time
explain: ROC-AUC measures ranking quality over all thresholds, not accuracy, recall or precision at one.

text: You try 200 hyperparameter settings and keep the best 5-fold CV score. That score is…
options: An unbiased estimate of the test score
Likely optimistic; check on held-out data
explain: The max of many noisy scores overfits the validation data, like chasing Leaderboard A.

text: What does logistic regression output before thresholding?
explain: It computes w·x + b and squashes it with the sigmoid into a probability between 0 and 1.

text: Why is logistic regression called a LINEAR classifier?
options: The sigmoid curve is a straight line
It is trained with MSE loss
It only works with one feature
Its decision boundary w·x + b = 0 is linear
explain: p > 0.5 exactly when w·x + b > 0, so the boundary is a line (hyperplane).

text: Class 1 = points inside a circle around (0, 0). How do you help logistic regression?
explain: x² + y² < r² is linear in the new features, so a linear model can now draw the circle.

text: Two features are near-copies of each other in linear regression. What happens?
options: The model can't be trained at all
Coefficients get unstable and hard to read
explain: Weight can shift between the twins (multicollinearity); predictions stay fine, and L2 (ridge) stabilises it.

text: Decision tree vs random forest: what is the key difference?
options: A forest averages many trees on resampled data
A forest is one very deep tree
A forest can only do regression
explain: Random forest = many trees on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets; their votes are averaged.

text: A decision tree with no max_depth limit usually…
explain: It keeps splitting until leaves are pure: near 100% train accuracy, worse validation.

text: How does a decision tree choose a split?
options: Randomly, keeping the first one tried
Makes child nodes as pure as possible
Uses the feature with the largest values
Makes both children the same size
explain: It picks the split that most reduces impurity (Gini or entropy) in the child nodes.

text: Bagging vs boosting?
options: Bagging is sequential, boosting is parallel
Same thing, only the names differ
Bagging: independent models; boosting: each fixes the last
Boosting works only with linear models
explain: Bagging averages independent models (cuts variance); boosting adds models that fix earlier errors (cuts bias).

text: Gradient boosting: validation loss is lowest at 300 trees, then rises. Best move?
explain: Too many boosting rounds overfit; early stopping keeps the best iteration.

text: Why does a random forest try only a random subset of features at each split?
options: To make each single tree more accurate
So no feature scaling is needed
explain: Less similar trees make different errors, so averaging them cancels more variance.

text: Gradient boosting with MSE loss: what is each new tree trained to predict?
options: The residuals of the current ensemble
A bootstrap sample of the targets
explain: Each tree fits what the model still gets wrong: the residuals (the negative gradient of MSE).

text: k-NN with k = 1 tends to…
explain: Every single point decides its own neighbourhood, so noise is memorised; larger k smooths the boundary.

text: What is the 'naive' assumption in Naive Bayes?
options: Features are independent given the class
explain: Given the class, features are treated as independent, so P(x|y) is a product of per-feature terms.

text: What does the kernel trick let an SVM do?
options: Use high-dim features without computing them
explain: A kernel gives dot products in a richer feature space directly, so the SVM gets non-linear boundaries cheaply.

text: In an SVM, a very large C means…
options: Wider margin, more training errors allowed
explain: C is the penalty for margin violations; a large C fits the training data hard and can overfit.

text: What must you choose before running k-means?
explain: k-means needs k up front; pick it with an elbow plot or the silhouette score.

text: The first principal component in PCA is the direction of…
explain: PCA finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance; standardise first so big units don't dominate.

text: k-means gives different clusters on two runs. Most likely cause?
explain: The result depends on the start; use k-means++ and several restarts (n_init).

text: Two moon-shaped clusters plus scattered noise points. Which method fits best?
explain: DBSCAN groups dense regions of any shape and labels outliers as noise; k-means assumes round blobs.

text: Train accuracy 99%, validation accuracy 70%. Diagnosis?
explain: A big train-validation gap means high variance: regularise, simplify, or get more data.

text: Which regularisation tends to set some weights exactly to zero?
explain: L1 pushes small weights to exactly 0 (feature selection); L2 only shrinks them.

text: Train and validation scores are both low and close. What should you try?
options: A more flexible model or better features
explain: This is underfitting (high bias): add capacity or features, or reduce regularisation.

text: In sklearn LogisticRegression, making C smaller gives…
explain: C is the INVERSE of regularisation strength: small C = strong penalty, simpler model.

text: You ran scaler.fit_transform(X_train). What do you call on X_test?
options: Nothing, test data needs no scaling
explain: transform reuses the train statistics; fit_transform on test is a leakage bug.

text: pandas: how do you count missing values in each column?
explain: isna() gives a True/False table and sum() counts the Trues per column.

text: Which call gives the scores you need for ROC-AUC (binary task)?
explain: ROC-AUC needs scores or probabilities for the positive class, not hard 0/1 labels.

text: What does stratify=y do in train_test_split?
options: Keeps class ratios the same in both splits
explain: Each split gets the same class proportions, which matters for small or imbalanced data.

text: Why put the scaler inside a Pipeline when running cross_val_score?
options: Pipelines skip scaling on test folds
Scaler is refit per training fold: no leakage
explain: Scaling all data before CV leaks the validation folds' stats; a Pipeline fits it inside each fold.

text: OneHotEncoder crashes on a city that appears only in the test set. Simple fix?
options: Refit the encoder on the test set
explain: Unknown categories become all-zero columns; refitting on test would break the column mapping.
